f.re: The following restrictions apply: - It is not permissible to anchor or operate boats in the prohibited areas for fishing, except in emergency cases resulting from weather conditions or a defect in the boat. - It is not permissible to drive a fishing boat except for those who hold a certificate from the Department of Ports and Lighthouses proving their eligibility for this and from the Public Authority for River Transport for fishing in inland waters. - It is not permissible to trap in the areas where it is prohibited to fish, or to fish with prohibited gear, and during fishing prohibitions determined by a decision of the Minister of Agriculture. - It is not permissible for a boat to fish in places other than those licensed to fish, nor may it fish in an unlicensed way without the approval of the General Authority for Fish Resources Development. - It is not permissible for the boat to have nets, machines or tools that are not licensed or prohibited for fishing, and no person may possess these machines and tools in or near the fishing sites. - It is not permissible to fish, sell or possess fish or other aquatic organisms in a fresh, dried or salted condition, whose lengths or sizes are less than the lengths and sizes specified by a decision of the Minister of Agriculture. - It is forbidden to take ornamental fish from marine waters except with a permit from the General Authority for Fish Resources Development. - Fish may not be disposed of within lakes and inland waters, and n…

Throughout the Greek Territory, the fishing and trading of crustaceans of the species Palinurus elephas (common spiny lobster) and Homarus gammarus (European lobster) is prohibited during the period from 1st September to 31st December of each year. f.re: The following restrictions apply: (a) No person will take fish employing the following methods: (1) Employing trawl nets in the Mediterranean Sea, if the length of the codend is less than 4 meters; Fisheries Regulations, 1937, paragraph 4(1). (2) In the Mediterranean rivers and within 100 meters of the mouth thereof, in a net, except in nets designated for fishing for mullet fry; For this matter, “fish fry” - a fish whose length from the tip of its mouth to the tip of its tail does not exceed 5 centimeters; Fisheries Regulations, 1937, paragraph 4(2). (3) By means of a fixed net or lattice or other fixed means. In this paragraph, “Fixed” means - anchored to the sea bed for a period of 7 days or more; Fisheries Regulations, 1937, paragraph 4(3). (4) Employing any means aimed at encouraging the movement of fish into the nets or traps, or to bring them out of hiding; Fisheries Regulations, 1937, paragraph 4(4). (5) By employing a long line in Lake Kinneret; Fisheries Regulations, 1937, paragraph 4(5). (6) By means of a spear gun in Lake Kinneret and in the Gulf of Eilat; Fisheries Regulations, 1937, paragraph 4(6). f.pu: To establish national maritime boundaries and manage the state's marine resources sustainably.
f.re: 1. No person may practice sport of diving unless he holds a diving certificate issued by a recognized diving training center. Diving activities must comply with the following conditions: (1) Diving must be conducted in areas that do not interfere with navigation routes; (2) Divers must display the internationally recognized diving flag indicating the presence of divers in the water; (3) The number of divers participating in a dive must correspond to the safety supervision capacity of the instructors. Diving shall be prohibited in the following areas: (1) Military zones; (2) Port areas and navigation channels: (3) Any other areas designated by the competent authorities for safety reasons. 2. The use of trawl nets is prohibited within Lebanese territorial waters at depths less than 250 meters. 3. It is prohibited to use fishing gear at a distance of less than 500 meters from beaches or bays, except for fishing practiced by foot. 4. The use of drag nets shall be prohibited at a distance of less than three nautical miles from the Lebanese coast.

Fishermen must, in the event that they capture any listed species alive, release them immediately after removing hooks (if present) from them in a manner that prevents them from being endangered. They must also throw dead animals immediately into the sea. Fishermen must, in the event that they capture any listed species, whether alive or dead, during fishing operations, inform the Department of Aquatic and Terrestrial Fishing or the regional services of the Ministry of Agriculture of the type and number of these animals. f.pu: To establish national maritime boundaries and manage fisheries resources.
f.re: The following restrictions apply: - All species of turtles and tortoises are protected. Any use of these species or thier products (skin, eggs, flesh) is banned. - Dumping of oils and other pollutants from vessels into the sea and discharge of land-based sewage and industrial water into the marine environment is prohibited. - It is prohibited to fish using explosives, toxic substances, drugs, substances harmful to public health, the growth or reproduction of marine organisms, or by any other means that harm marine creatures without discrimination. - Dredging for sponges is prohibited. - all fishing activities, foreign or domestic, must be licensed and authorized. It is prohibited to fish in marinas, ports and shipping lanes leading to them. - It is prohibited to harm the seaweeds and plants in which marine organisms lay eggs. Additional restrictions, such as bag limits, seasons, and size restrictions may apply. Please consult the local fishing laws for more information.

During periods and in areas where trawling is prohibited, bottom trawl nets may be transported if stored properly onboard. Trawl doors may not be hung. If stored, the ends (matafora) where doors are suspended must face inside the vessel. During prohibited periods, it is forbidden to keep unsealed trawl nets and doors in ports, shelters, mooring, and dry dock areas.
